name: Bali
tagline: Temple-strewn rice terraces, surf coasts and spiritual calm.
whenBlurb: Come April through October for the dry season and clear coast; skip November to March, when heavy afternoon rain settles in.

ourTake.lede: Bali is really several islands in one, and the mistake is trying to do all of it; pick two bases and stay put. Ubud for culture and rice terraces, and a southern beach or the Bukit for the coast, is the classic pairing that still works. Avoid the traffic-choked Kuta-Seminyak strip if you can, and if your dates land on Nyepi, embrace it, the whole island shuts in silence and it's extraordinary.
ourTake.comeIf: You want cliff-edge villas, ricefield calm and a honeymoon that balances beach with real culture.
ourTake.skipIf: You want a short, easy hop; the flight is long and the south can be crowded.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

credentials: World Travel Awards, Indonesia's Leading Lifestyle Resort 2025
Travel + Leisure, Best Hotel Pools in Indonesia 2026

items.name: Uluwatu Temple & the Kecak Fire Dance at sunset
items.description: A 11th-century sea temple perched on a cliff 70 metres above the Indian Ocean, where a hundred bare-chested men chant the Ramayana in the round as the sun drops behind the stage. For Indian families the story is instantly familiar, Rama, Sita, Ravana, Hanuman, which makes the hypnotic 'cak-cak-cak' rhythm land deeper. Have your driver arrive by 5pm for the good seats.

items.name: Tanah Lot, the floating sea temple
items.description: A 16th-century shrine on a black-rock islet that appears to float at high tide, one of Indonesia's most photographed silhouettes at sunset. The clifftop terraces let elders watch the light change in comfort while younger travellers walk down to the tide pools; a private driver-plus-guide turns the crowd into a manageable golden hour.

items.name: Besakih, the Mother Temple
items.description: Bali's largest and holiest Hindu complex, 23 temples terraced up the flank of Mount Agung, in use for over a thousand years and unharmed by the 1963 eruption that stopped at its steps. For Hindu travellers this is the spiritual heart of the island; a licensed guide explains the pura hierarchy and keeps the temple touts at bay.

items.name: Tirta Empul holy-spring purification (Melukat)
items.description: A sacred water temple founded in 962 AD where Balinese Hindus queue at carved spouts for Melukat, a purification ritual to cleanse mind and spirit. It resonates powerfully for Indian travellers who know the idea of holy-water darshan; a private guide (now required for the ritual) arranges a quiet early slot and a sarong, so it feels devotional rather than touristic.

items.name: Lempuyang Temple, the Gates of Heaven
items.description: A hilltop temple where two split gates frame Mount Agung to perfection, the island's most famous photograph (the 'water reflection' is a mirror trick the on-site photographer performs under the lens). Come before sunrise, before cloud swallows the volcano; a driver who leaves Ubud at 4am beats both the heat and the two-hour queue.

items.name: Jatiluwih rice terraces & the Subak system
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Cultural Landscape of Bali Province: the Subak System as a Manifestation of the Tri Hita Karana Philosophy
items.description: Over 600 hectares of emerald terraces sculpted by a thousand-year-old cooperative irrigation system rooted in the Tri Hita Karana philosophy of harmony between people, nature and the divine. Cooler, quieter and far grander than the roadside terraces near Ubud, a walking trail and a warung lunch make an unhurried half-day for a private group.

items.name: Tegallalang rice terraces & the jungle swings
items.description: The classic stepped valley just 20 minutes north of Ubud, clean paths, coconut palms and the giant swings that arc out over the paddies, catnip for teenagers and grandparents with a camera alike. Go early (before 8am) with a driver so you get the low-angle light and the terraces largely to yourselves.

items.name: Sacred Monkey Forest Sanctuary
items.description: A 12.5-hectare jungle reserve in the heart of Ubud with three moss-covered 14th-century temples and 1,200 long-tailed macaques the Balinese hold sacred. A hit with multi-generational groups, just leave sunglasses and loose bags in the car, as the monkeys are quick and cheeky.

items.name: Campuhan Ridge Walk at dawn
items.description: A gentle two-kilometre spine of grassy ridge above a green valley, the loveliest free thing to do in Ubud, best walked at 6am when it is cool, soft-lit and nearly empty. Easy enough for most of the family, and a coffee stop at the top rewards the effort before the day heats up.

items.name: Ubud Royal Palace & evening Legong / Barong dance
items.description: The 19th-century Puri Saren Agung, still home to Ubud's royal family, hosts nightly traditional dance in its courtyard, Legong, the Ramayana ballet, or the Barong's battle of good and evil, set to live gamelan. Free to wander by day; an evening performance under the carved gates is the most accessible window into Balinese court culture.

items.name: Ubud Art Market
items.description: Across the road from the palace, a warren of stalls for ikat sarongs, woven baskets, silver and carved wood, good fun to browse and haggle, with your guide steering you to the better-quality vendors upstairs. A relaxed hour for the family before or after the dance.

items.name: ARMA, Agung Rai Museum of Art
items.description: A serene garden museum founded by a Balinese collector, spanning classical Kamasan bark painting, the celebrated 1930s Batuan and Pita Maha works, and foreign masters who fell for the island. The calmest, best-curated art stop in Ubud, and its cultural workshops (painting, dance) are a genuine private-hosted experience for older children.

items.name: Neka Art Museum
items.description: Six pavilions telling the chronological story of Balinese painting and its collision with visiting Western artists, arguably the most historically grounded collection on the island. Air-conditioned, unhurried and easy to pair with a Campuhan walk on the same morning.

items.name: Blanco Renaissance Museum
items.description: The flamboyant clifftop house-studio of Filipino-Spanish painter Don Antonio Blanco, perched above the Campuhan gorge with gilded frames, ornate architecture and river views. A quick, characterful stop, half art, half theatre, that photographs beautifully.

items.name: Mount Batur sunrise trek
items.description: A 2am start and a torch-lit climb up an active volcano to watch dawn break over the caldera and Lake Batur, with a hot-spring soak to follow. Best for the fitter, adventurous members of the family; a private guide, hot tea at the summit and a slower pace make it far more civilised than the group tours.

items.name: Kintamani caldera lunch with Mount Batur views
items.description: For those who'd rather not climb at 2am, the ridge restaurants of Kintamani deliver the whole caldera, volcano, black lava fields and lake, over a leisurely lunch. Cool mountain air, a private driver and a table on the rim make an effortless half-day from Ubud.

items.name: Ulun Danu Beratan, the lake temple
items.description: A 17th-century temple dedicated to the water goddess Dewi Danu, its multi-tiered meru shrines appearing to float on misty Lake Beratan at 1,200 metres. The cool highland setting is a gentle, photogenic stop for all ages, and unmistakably the temple on the 50,000-rupiah note.

items.name: Munduk waterfalls & the highland trails
items.description: A cool, cloud-forest village of clove and coffee plantations laced with jungle waterfall walks, the un-touristy alternative to Bali's crowded cascades. A guided morning trek here, ending in a country lunch, suits families who want green calm over beach heat.

items.name: Twin Lakes, Buyan & Tamblingan
items.description: Two serene crater lakes inside an extinct volcano, once a single body of water, now separated by a jungle land-bridge you can trek between past mossy shrines. A traditional dugout canoe crossing on Tamblingan is a quiet, storybook experience away from the crowds.

items.name: Sekumpul Waterfall
items.description: Widely rated Bali's most spectacular falls, a fan of seven cascades over 80 metres tall, reached by a 400-step jungle descent and a river crossing. It rewards effort with drama; for a softer version, a guide can position you at the viewpoint without the full scramble.

items.name: Tegenungan Waterfall
items.description: A powerful 15-metre curtain of water just 20 minutes from Ubud, the easiest 'proper' waterfall to reach, with a stepped path and a swimmable pool at the base. Best before 8am for light and space; an easy add-on to a Ubud rice-terrace morning.

items.name: Sidemen Valley & ikat weaving
items.description: The Bali that Ubud used to be, hand-tended rice terraces cascading toward Mount Agung, birdsong instead of scooters, and family workshops still weaving endek and songket ikat the old way. The most restful base on the island for a private villa; walk the paddies at dawn, watch a loom in the afternoon.

items.name: Celuk village silversmithing
items.description: Bali's 'silver village', where families have hand-worked gold and silver for generations, chisel, punch and granulation done at the bench in front of you. Book a private smithing session to design and make your own piece, or commission investment jewellery direct from the maker.

items.name: Balinese cooking class
items.description: Start with a dawn market walk for lemongrass, galangal and torch ginger, then grind your own bumbu base and cook a full Balinese spread over a shared table. Ubud's classes are famously vegetarian-friendly, a warm, hands-on afternoon that travels home with the family.

items.name: Kelingking Beach & the T-Rex cliff
credentials: Ranked among The World's 50 Best Beaches (2024)
items.description: The dinosaur-shaped limestone headland that put Nusa Penida on every screen, a jaw of cliff plunging to a turquoise cove, one of the world's most jaw-dropping viewpoints. Reach it as a fast-boat day trip from Sanur; the viewpoint alone is worth it (the steep climb to the sand is optional and only for the sure-footed).

items.name: Angel's Billabong & Broken Beach
items.description: A natural infinity rock-pool carved by the sea, beside an arched cliff-tunnel where the ocean churns through a hidden bay, two of Nusa Penida's most surreal formations, side by side. A private car-and-boat day keeps the island's rough roads and crowds off your itinerary.

items.name: Diamond Beach
items.description: A postcard cove of jagged white sea-stacks, bright sand and electric-blue water on Penida's quieter east coast, the island's most beautiful beach. Best admired from the clifftop terraces; the sculpted staircase down is dramatic but steep, so it suits the adventurous.

items.name: Nusa Lembongan, mantas, mangroves & Devil's Tear
items.description: The gentler, easier Nusa island, snorkel with harmless four-metre manta rays at Manta Bay, drift the mangroves, and watch the Devil's Tear blowholes explode at sunset. Calmer roads and clearer water than Penida make it the family-friendly island day from Bali.

items.name: Padang Padang Beach
items.description: A jewel-box cove reached through a cleft in the rock, its shallow left-hand reef home to the Rip Curl Cup and Indonesia's most photographed wave. Small and lovely for a morning swim and sunbathe; the surf is expert-only, but the setting is for everyone.

items.name: Bingin Beach & the Bukit cliffs
items.description: A dramatic wall of cliff, a fast reef break beloved by surfers, and a white-sand strip reached by steep stairs, the raw, cinematic side of the Bukit peninsula. Come for the clifftop view and the barrelling waves; a villa above Bingin buys you the whole coastline as a backdrop.

items.name: Uluwatu clifftop beach clubs
items.description: Bali's most theatrical sundowners, Single Fin's deck over Suluban, Ulu Cliffhouse's mid-century terrace, or Savaya's glass-and-marble stage 100 metres above the surf, all facing due west. A private table for the family as the sun melts into the Indian Ocean is Bukit at its most glamorous.

items.name: Jimbaran Bay seafood on the sand
items.description: Choose your fish, prawns and lobster from the ice, then eat it grilled over coconut husk at a lantern-lit table with your feet almost in the water, sunset ahead. A Bali rite of passage, book a private table for 5–6pm and let a driver handle the crescent of restaurants.

items.name: Nusa Dua's calm beaches
items.description: The island's most sheltered, resort-lined coast, soft sand, gentle reef-protected water and manicured promenades, ideal for grandparents and small children who want the sea without the surf. The base of choice when the priority is easy, safe swimming and space to breathe.

items.name: Seminyak, beach, boutiques & sunset dining
items.description: Bali's most polished stretch of coast, designer boutiques, spas and a long west-facing beach lined with sundowner tables and beach clubs. The easy, cosmopolitan counterpoint to the temples and terraces, and a good first or last base close to the airport.

items.name: The Yoga Barn
items.description: One of Southeast Asia's largest yoga and healing centres, daily classes in every style, sound baths, meditation and a vegan garden café, all in a jungle setting. A discreet, drop-in way to fold wellness into an Ubud stay without committing to a full retreat.

items.name: Fivelements Retreat spa day
items.description: A riverside holistic sanctuary on the sacred Ayung, famed for Balinese healing rituals, plant-based cuisine and a bamboo-and-water architecture that has won it dozens of global wellness awards. A private spa day here is the island's most refined reset, deeply veg-friendly and utterly serene.

items.name: Ayung River white-water rafting
items.description: A scenic Class II–III float down the Ayung through jungle gorge, past carved rock walls and hidden waterfalls, thrilling enough for teenagers, gentle enough for confident parents. The most family-friendly adrenaline on the island, run by well-established operators.

items.name: Goa Gajah, the Elephant Cave
items.description: A 9th–11th-century sanctuary with a menacing carved cave mouth, ancient bathing pools and both Hindu and Buddhist relics in the same grove. A quick, atmospheric archaeological stop that pairs naturally with Tirta Empul on a temple-focused morning.

items.name: Tukad Cepung, the cave waterfall
items.description: A slot-canyon cascade where midday light beams through the rock onto falling water, deep in a hidden gorge, one of Bali's most surreal photographs. A short, wet walk through the canyon makes it a fun mini-adventure for older children.

items.name: Batur natural hot springs
items.description: Mineral pools fed by volcanic springs on the shore of Lake Batur, looking straight up at the caldera, the traditional reward after a sunrise climb, but worth it on its own. A warm, restorative soak in the cool mountains, easy for every generation.

items.name: Melasti Beach
items.description: A sweep of white sand at the foot of towering carved limestone cliffs, reached by a dramatic cut-through road, one of the Bukit's cleanest, calmest swims. Quieter than Padang Padang and grand enough for a private beach morning.

items.name: Gili Islands day escape
items.description: Three car-free, scooter-free specks of powder-white sand off Lombok, ringed by coral and green turtles, you get around by bicycle or horse-drawn cidomo. A fast boat from Bali delivers a day of snorkelling at Turtle Point and Coral Garden; Gili Meno and Gili Air are the serenest for families.

items.name: Locavore NXT
items.description: A forage-to-table 'localised rebellion', the most progressive kitchen in Indonesia, built on its own food system.

items.name: Room4Dessert
credentials: The World's 50 Best Restaurants, World's Best Pastry Chef 2021 (Will Goldfarb)
items.description: Will Goldfarb's dessert-led tasting theatre, the ex-elBulli mind who was named the world's best pastry chef.

items.name: Kayuputi
credentials: Wine Spectator Best of Award of Excellence (16th consecutive year, 2025)
items.description: Pan-Asian haute cuisine on the Nusa Dua beachfront, with one of Bali's most decorated cellars.

items.name: Mozaic
credentials: Former World's 50 Best Restaurants listing (Chef Chris Salans)
items.description: The restaurant that brought fine dining to Ubud, a quarter-century of French technique and Indonesian flavour.

items.name: Merah Putih
items.description: High-end Indonesian archipelago cooking under cathedral-like ceilings, arguably Bali's most beautiful room.

items.name: Cuca
items.description: A garden restaurant of Indonesian-sourced small plates and tapas, playful, ingredient-led, much-garlanded.

items.name: Sangsaka
items.description: A small, fire-driven kitchen doing one of the island's most exciting modern-Indonesian tasting menus.

items.name: Sarong
credentials: Recognised among Asia's best (Chef Will Meyrick)
items.description: Chef Will Meyrick's street-food-to-fine-dining journey across Asia, glamorous and generous.

items.name: Mamasan
items.description: Will Meyrick's other room, 1920s-Shanghai theatre and bold pan-Asian street flavours.

items.name: Métis
items.description: Grand French-Mediterranean dining over the rice fields, a long-standing Seminyak occasion address.

items.name: Bambu
items.description: Fine Indonesian dining in a lantern-lit garden pavilion, one of Seminyak's most atmospheric rooms.

items.name: Sundara
credentials: Four Seasons, group dining standard; Travel + Leisure Jimbaran Bay honours
items.description: A beach club and grill on Jimbaran Bay, sunset, seafood and Four Seasons polish.

items.name: Api Jiwa
items.description: An open-fire chef's-counter grilling over Indonesian binchotan and flame, smoke, char and craft.

items.name: Ijen at Desa Potato Head
credentials: Within Desa Potato Head, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 18)
items.description: A zero-waste, fire-led tasting kitchen inside Bali's most awarded design hotel.

items.name: Mauri
items.description: A refined Italian-leaning fine-dining newcomer that has climbed straight to the island's best-of lists.

items.name: Barbacoa
items.description: Latin-American open-fire and wood-smoke cooking in a soaring warehouse, bold, generous, fun.

items.name: Hujan Locale
items.description: Will Meyrick's Ubud house for regional Indonesian home cooking, unfussy, warm, deeply of-the-island.

items.name: Kaum
credentials: Within Desa Potato Head, World's 50 Best Hotels 2025 (No. 18)
items.description: Heritage Indonesian recipes gathered from across the archipelago, cooking with a preservation mission.

items.name: Night Rooster
credentials: Sister venue to Locavore NXT, Asia's 50 Best Restaurants 2026 (No. 44)
items.description: Locavore's cocktail bar, theatrical, botanical drinks built on Indonesian folklore and native ingredients.

items.name: Bridges Bali
items.description: A river-gorge restaurant and wine cellar spanning the Campuhan bridges, a long-standing Ubud institution.

items.name: Bella Cibo
items.description: Considered Italian cooking on the Canggu coast, a quiet favourite that keeps its standards high.

items.name: Warung Babi Guling Ibu Oka
items.description: Ubud's most famous suckling-pig warung, the honest, non-negotiable taste of Balinese food.

items.name: Potato Head Beach Club
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars, Sustainable Bar Award (2018)
items.description: The amphitheatre of shutters facing the sunset, the beach club that set the island's standard, and cleaned up its act too.

items.name: 40 Thieves
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars 2025, No. 99 (51–100 extended list)
items.description: A hidden speakeasy above a ramen counter, tight, skilled cocktails and a room that tends to end up dancing.

items.name: Night Rooster
credentials: Asia's 50 Best Bars, 50 Best Discovery (Night Rooster by Locavore NXT)
items.description: Locavore's planter's-club bar, where Bali's 'king of cocktails' builds drinks on fermented island fruit and homemade bitters.

items.name: Rock Bar
credentials: Travel + Leisure, one of the World's Coolest Hotel Bars (No. 4)
items.description: A glass bar bolted to the rocks above the Indian Ocean, reached by its own cliff inclinator, the island's great sundowner.

items.name: Savaya
credentials: DJ Mag Top 100 Clubs 2025, No. 6 in the World, No. 1 in Asia
items.description: A clifftop stage a hundred metres above the ocean, drawing the world's headline DJs to Bali's southern tip.

plan.heading: 5 days in Bali, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Arrive at Four Seasons Sayan or Amandari above the Ayung gorge, and take breakfast over the river.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A private walk through the Tegallalang rice terraces late in the day, then the water temple at Pura Tirta Empul.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Mozaic, Chef Chris Salans' long-running fine-dining room in Ubud.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Meet a wood-carver in Mas or a silversmith in Celuk, then the Neka Art Museum for Balinese painting.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A guided offering-making session or a temple blessing arranged privately, followed by spa time.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Room4Dessert, Will Goldfarb's tasting counter, then a walk through Ubud's evening lanes.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive east to the water palace at Tirta Gangga and the terraced village of Sidemen, quieter than the south.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch with a view of Mount Agung, then transfer to the coast.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Check in at a Bukit or Uluwatu villa; dinner at Sundara or a private chef at the villa.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning swim, then the clifftop temple of Pura Luhur Uluwatu before the crowds.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Beach time at a Bingin or Padang Padang day club, or a surf lesson for the willing.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at Bambu or Merah Putih back toward Seminyak, then a nightcap on the cliffs.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A long spa morning and a final swim.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: A slow lunch of babi guling or fresh seafood at Jimbaran.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Sunset drinks at Rock Bar before the airport transfer.

items.name: Ubud
items.description: The cultural heart amid rice terraces and temples; for art, wellness and greenery over beaches.

items.name: Uluwatu / the Bukit
items.description: Cliff-top resorts and surf beaches on the southern peninsula; for dramatic coast and privacy.

items.name: Seminyak / Canggu
items.description: The beach-club, dining and shopping strip; lively and social, if increasingly busy and traffic-heavy.

events.name: Nyepi (Day of Silence)
events.note: The Balinese New Year, preceded by the Ogoh-Ogoh effigy parades and followed by a full day when the entire island falls silent.

events.name: Bali Arts Festival
events.note: A month-long celebration of Balinese dance, music and craft centred on Denpasar; the island's cultural high point.

events.name: Galungan & Kuningan
events.note: The most important Balinese holy days, when penjor bamboo poles line the streets and temples fill with offerings.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Match the setting to the mood, Ubud for jungle and culture, the Bukit peninsula (Uluwatu) for clifftop calm; a sarong is required at temples, and Indian passport holders receive visa-on-arrival, so confirm it before flying.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: You arrive at Ngurah Rai (DPS); a private car with driver meets you and reaches Seminyak in thirty minutes or Ubud in about ninety, and a helicopter transfer avoids the south's traffic entirely.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: Keep a private car and driver for the day, as distances are long and roads are slow; walk within Ubud or a beach enclave and use resort shuttles for the immediate area.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: A Telkomsel eSIM gives reliable 4G across the south and Ubud; wifi is strong in villas and resorts.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: Indonesian rupiah (IDR); cards are accepted at hotels and better restaurants but cash is needed for drivers, temples and warungs; round up or leave a small tip.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: The dry season from April to October brings warm, low-humidity days; avoid the wet season, worst in December and January, when heavy downpours and humidity settle over the island.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi in about 8h on Air India or IndiGo; from Mumbai it is one connection, typically via Singapore, Kuala Lumpur or Bangkok, where Singapore Airlines and Thai offer the strongest business cabins and lounges. For a first-class feel, connect through Singapore.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No mandatory vaccinations; Hepatitis A and Typhoid advised, and confirm routine jabs. Generally safe. Drink bottled water only and be careful with ice and raw produce, as stomach upsets are common. No altitude concern at the resorts.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Excellent for vegetarians; plant-based dining is a genuine strength of the island, and Jain is workable with instruction. Indian food is available in Seminyak and Ubud. Locavore and the vegetarian tables in Ubud are notable; Gterrace and Queen's Tandoor cover Indian cravings.
